previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell activation syndrome and recent CABG was admitted for substernal chest pressure and leg cramps. She attributed her symptoms to a mast cell flare, possibly triggered by hypokalemia and stress. Initial evaluation showed a potassium level of 3.0 mEq/L, which was corrected with oral and IV supplementation. Serial troponins were negative, EKGs unchanged, and chest imaging showed no acute cardiopulmonary process. Her symptoms improved with administration of her standard mast cell protocol, including IV Benadryl, Ativan, and Dilaudid. She remained stable on telemetry, with gradual resolution of chest pressure. She was discharged home with potassium supplements and plans for follow-up with her allergist and cardiologist.
problems: Malignant mast cell tumors, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites

tertiary contractions were noted in the distal esophagus with barium pooling
in the mid and lower esophagus, which cleared only once the patient was
repositioned upright.  There was no esophageal mass. The esophageal mucosa
appear normal.

No evidence of esophageal stricture or narrowing.  No hiatal hernia or reflux
was noted during this examination.  The patient is s/p ___ myotomy and
fundoplication.  A recurrent hiatal hernia is noted.  The wrap is intact.

A 13 mm barium tablet was administered, which was noted to holdup at the
gastroesophageal junction for several minutes but eventually passed into the
stomach.

No overt abnormality in the stomach or duodenum on limited evaluation.

seen in the distal portion the esophagus.

2.  Hiatal hernia, s/p fundoplication.  There is Holdup of a 13 mm barium
tablet at the gastroesophageal junction for several minutes, however
eventually the tablet passes into the stomach.

3. Approximately 5 minutes after completing this study, the patient complained
of worsening chest pain and wheezing.  The patient received nebulizer
treatment and was stabilized with nursing staff.  Patient additional received
an Epipen at approximately 10:45 and was noted to be hemodynamically stable
following the above interventions.
